input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I haven’t been able to send those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—for a few hours now. I’m not sure what’s wrong, but I’d really like to get it working again. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I can see that my phone shows a signal with just one bar and it says 2G at the top. Mobile data looks like it’s on, and my battery is at 80%. I haven’t noticed any specific error messages when I try to send a picture message—it just doesn’t go through.

I’m not sure about browsing the web, but I can try if you need me to. Regular calls seem to work, though. What should I do next?

Oh, I just checked, and it looks like my phone is set to use only 2G. I don’t really know how to change that to 4G or 5G. Could you please give me step-by-step instructions? I get a bit nervous with these settings, so simple steps would really help.

Alright, I followed your instructions and changed the setting. Now my phone shows a strong signal and says 5G at the top, so I think it worked. But I just tried sending a picture message again, and it still won’t go through. 

Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working?

I checked, and my phone shows that mobile data is on, and I’m not connected to Wi-Fi. Wi-Fi Calling is also turned off. 

Would you like me to try browsing a website to see if mobile data is working, or is there something else I should check?
I tried to check if I could browse the internet, but it looks like there’s no connection at all—it didn’t work. Does this mean my mobile data isn’t working? What should I do now?

I found something called APN settings on my phone. It says the APN name is “internet” and there’s a MMSC URL listed as well. I’m not sure if these are correct or if I need to change anything. Should I reset these settings, or is there something else I should do? I get a bit nervous changing things I don’t understand.

I’m a bit worried about resetting things—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I reset the APN settings or restart my phone? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you please reassure me about what will happen, and then I’ll try to follow your instructions?

Alright, I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you suggested. You mentioned I need to restart my phone now—just to double-check, restarting won’t erase anything, right? I’m always a bit anxious about that. If it’s safe, I’ll go ahead and restart.

I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t browse the internet and picture messages still won’t send. I’m starting to feel a bit frustrated—why isn’t this fixing it? Is there anything else we can try?

Yes, please, I think that would be best. I’m feeling a bit overwhelmed with all of this, and I just want to get it working again. Thank you for your help so far—please transfer me to someone who can look into it more closely.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

1. Open the “Settings” app on your phone.
2. Look for a section called “Connections,” “Network & Internet,” or “Mobile Network.” Tap on it.

5. Tap on it, and you should see options like “2G,” “3G,” “4G,” or “5G.”
6. Select “4G/5G preferred” or “4G/3G/2G (auto connect)” if available.

To be sure, the safest next step is to reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. This often resolves issues like the one you’re experiencing, and it’s a standard troubleshooting step.
